```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
set.seed(2026)
library(IRTistic)
```

`IRTistic` puts model fitting, diagnostics and graphics for item response
theory (IRT) and Rasch measurement in one place. Every analysis follows the
same pattern:

1. fit a model (`irt_fit()` or `mfrm_fit()`),
2. inspect it with tables (`summary()`, `item_fit()`, `facet_report()`, ...),
3. draw it with `plot()` or a `plot_*()` function. Plots are ggplot objects,
   so you can add `facet_wrap()`, themes or labels as usual.

## Dichotomous and polytomous IRT

```{r}
dat <- sim_irt(500, nitems = 10, model = "rasch")
fit <- irt_fit(dat, model = "rasch")
summary(fit)
```

Person measures by EAP, MAP, ML or WLE:

```{r}
head(irt_scores(fit, "WLE"))
```

Rasch-style infit/outfit statistics are available for every model:

```{r}
item_fit(fit)
```

```{r}
plot(fit, "wright")
plot(fit, "fit")
plot(fit, "icc", items = 1:6)
```

Polytomous models (`"grm"`, `"pcm"`, `"gpcm"`, `"rsm"`) and mixed tests work
the same way:

```{r}
poly <- sim_irt(500, nitems = 6, model = "grm", ncat = 4)
fg <- irt_fit(poly, "grm", se = "none")
plot(fg, "icc")
plot(fg, "info")
```

Compare nested models with a likelihood-ratio test:

```{r}
d2 <- sim_irt(500, 8, "2pl")
anova(irt_fit(d2, "rasch", se = "none"), irt_fit(d2, "2pl", se = "none"))
```

### Assumption checks

```{r}
local_dependence(fit)
residual_pca(fit)
```

### Differential item functioning

```{r}
group <- rep(c("A", "B"), 250)
dif <- dif_test(fit, group, method = "mh")
plot_dif(dif)
```

### Multidimensional models

Supply a Q-matrix of loadings:

```{r}
Q <- cbind(rep(1:0, each = 5), rep(0:1, each = 5))
md <- sim_irt(600, 10, "2pl", Q = Q, Sigma = matrix(c(1, .5, .5, 1), 2))
fm <- irt_fit(md, "2pl", Q = Q, se = "none")
fm$Sigma
```

## Many-facet Rasch measurement (FACETS-style)

Rater-mediated data come in long format, one row per rating:

```{r}
ratings <- sim_mfrm(n_person = 80, n_rater = 5, n_criterion = 4, design = 0.8)
head(ratings)
mf <- mfrm_fit(ratings, person = "person", facets = c("rater", "criterion"), score = "score")
mf
```

The measurement report gives each facet's measures, standard errors, fair
averages, fit, and separation/reliability, plus the category statistics:

```{r}
facet_report(mf)
```

```{r, fig.height = 5.5}
plot(mf, "facets")
plot(mf, "categories")
plot(mf, "fit")
```

Rater-by-criterion bias (interaction) analysis:

```{r}
bias <- mfrm_bias(mf, c("rater", "criterion"))
bias
plot_bias(bias)
```
